title: Endpoint variation test is not actually parametrized
reasoning: The method name and signature imply it should exercise multiple endpoint variations, but unittest/Django TestCase will invoke it only once using the default arguments. No test calls it with a non-empty query string or a culmination feast name, so those branches and the pluralized countdown path are not covered by the suite despite being embedded in the test body.
recommendation: Split the branches into separate test methods or convert the file to pytest parametrization with explicit cases for no query params, query params, and culmination-feast countdown behavior.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Because the optional parameters are never supplied by the test runner, only the default path runs.
suggestedRegressionTest: Create explicit tests such as test_fast_on_date_default_countdown and test_fast_on_date_culmination_feast_countdown that assert each expected response independently.

history.reasoning: The original evidence still exists at `tests/integration/test_endpoints.py:51-88`. The test is still defined as `def test_fast_on_date_endpoint_variations(self, query_params='', culmination_feast_name=None):`, so Django/unittest will execute it once with the default arguments and never supply the non-default `query_params` or `culmination_feast_name` values. A repository-wide search found no other tests that call this method or independently assert the `?date=20240325` path or the culmination-feast countdown branch. Those branches remain behaviorally distinct in current code: `hub/serializers.py:217-235` has separate countdown logic for `culmination_feast` vs. normal fast end dates. I attempted to run the targeted Django test via the project’s documented Docker command, but the app container was not running, so there is no passing test evidence to contradict the finding.
